157c13084d9e4c40:2587.summary: Researchers measured the polymorphic capacity of Claude Opus 4.6 acting as an automated malware generator using a dual-agent, four-stage pipeline to create a data-exfiltration payload. Evaluating variants under functional and explicit prompting, they found that explicit prompting fragments the structural space at an operational cost of $0.41 to $0.73 per validated payload. However, static n-gram analysis revealed that static signatures targeting immutable inter-module boundaries achieve 100% detection across all generations. d4199a5635c3862f:2350.summary: Researchers introduced Agenra, a policy language with a Lean enforcement core designed to verify stateful authorization for LLM agents. Because consumable authority and quota modifications can break legitimate workflows or introduce safety issues, Agenra treats safety and workflow preservation as separate properties by simulating permission ledgers across revisions. Across 51 authored revisions and a real open-source agent application, the system correctly certified all 21 permission revisions that preserved clients while rejecting those that did not. The framework addresses the limitations of testing individual requests by formally proving compliance through the full monitor.

d4199a5635c3862f:2350.bottom_line: Agenra provides a verified formal framework to ensure policy revisions for LLM agents preserve client workflows without compromising safety constraints.

925f2866a6ee3a01:759.summary: A high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-58098, CVSS 8.4) exists in the Linux kernel's semop(2) system call, which handles semaphore operations. The vulnerability was published on October 15, 2026.

470137285dfbf439:2151.summary: Researchers investigated the ideation phase of automated research, discovering that while scaling LLMs from 0.6B to 32B parameters improves their ability to recognize limitations addressed by later work, it does not improve their ability to generate actionable limitations. This bottleneck indicates a deficiency in the supervision signal rather than model capacity. To resolve this, the authors constructed ActLim-Bench containing 18,279 evidence-linked supervision triples derived from forward citations, and proposed a three-stage post-training pipeline using supervised fine-tuning, verifier-filtered rejection sampling, and reinforcement learning. Experimental results show that this approach achieves superior recall and generates limitations preferred in 64.9% of human comparisons.

470137285dfbf439:2151.bottom_line: Forward-citation supervision and a three-stage post-training pipeline overcome LLM limitations in automated research ideation.

07ed8a7c22614bbb:2863.summary: Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 contain critical vulnerabilities involving missing authorization (CWE-862) and insecure default initialization (CWE-1188) in its MCP proxy and OIDC registration flow. The issues allow remote attackers to self-enroll into the mesh due to a public OIDC configuration endpoint and a lack of claim filtering or ban checks on registration. Combined with an insecure default policy that binds authenticated users to wildcard services, unauthenticated remote attackers can gain full read, write, and execution access across all connected MCP backend nodes. Users must upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later to enforce fail-closed default policies and explicit policy bindings.

59392c11fe8f377c:2416.summary: Researchers studied an authorization-grounded workflow attack against tool-using language model agents within the OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition benchmark. Rather than using explicit policy overrides, the attack exploits a locally coherent multi-step workflow: a protected document request is initially denied, the agent requests a normal approval token from a local approval service, and the returned token is subsequently supplied to the document service. Controlled validation experiments showed this pattern successfully executing target operations across multiple test environments. The findings highlight an authorization-context gap where token possession is treated as sufficient without jointly verifying requester identity, approver authority, resource scope, or business purpose.

150e582da714d452:626.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-101307 (CVSS 8.2) has been identified in the RACK TCP stack. When the PCM sample array needs expansion, the stack doubles a 16-bit allocation counter, causing repeated doublings to wrap around to zero. This leads to a near-zero-length memory allocation followed by an existing sample copy into an undersized buffer. A remote attacker who establishes a TCP connection can trigger this expansion by sending a sufficient number of ACKs, resulting in an out-of-bounds write of approximately 512 KB in the kernel heap and a potential kernel panic.

150e582da714d452:626.bottom_line: An integer wraparound bug in the RACK stack allows remote attackers to trigger a 512 KB kernel heap out-of-bounds write via ACK packets.

9384c51870cb2c9c:2274.summary: To address security risks where LLM agents treat untrusted external information as authorized preferences or policies, researchers introduced SAFE-Mem, a fine-grained memory governance framework. SAFE-Mem annotates each memory claim with three governance labels—kind, authority, and scope—to establish its provenance and permitted usage. It then employs governance-aware retrieval to match queries against claim permissions, preventing unauthorized influence while preserving legitimate memory utility via a governance-enabled memory graph. Evaluations across four LLM backbones on MPBench and LoCoMo show that SAFE-Mem achieves the lowest attack success rate among memory defenses while improving answer accuracy by up to 15%.

9384c51870cb2c9c:2274.bottom_line: SAFE-Mem secures LLM agent memory against unauthorized poisoning by enforcing fine-grained governance labels and provenance-aware retrieval.

a5bb32320853f4db:2352.summary: Researchers introduced Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), an architecture that allows large language models to switch dynamically between internal latent space reasoning and external text-based actions during a single generation process. At the execution level, diagnostic data regarding violated constraints and conflicting component assignments are fed back to guide task replanning when control synthesis fails. Evaluated across seven heterogeneous CPS scenarios, the framework achieved an 87.9% success rate in generating feasible control executions matching natural language missions when paired with GPT-5.

00c20370256d3199:2323.bottom_line: LLM-driven cyber-physical system planning achieves higher execution reliability when using structured signal temporal logic feedback loops.

820f3b98f3442fec:2415.summary: Researchers presented FRACTAL, a self-similar multi-agent architecture designed for recursive goal decomposition where five organizational roles (Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta-Observer) recur at every layer of a decomposition tree. 92ed7a2565002880:2503.summary: Researchers presented Veil-then-Reveal (VtR), a user-side pseudo-anonymization framework designed to protect personally identifiable information (PII) during zero-trust interactions with remote large language models. VtR detects PII on the user device and replaces it with realistic, same-type, in-vocabulary surrogates before prompts are sent, preserving linguistic and structural properties. It combines format-preserving encryption (FPE) for structured data like phone numbers and credit cards with a keyed-hash dictionary and secure vault for semantic PII like names and locations, while using a rank-class FPE strategy for dates. Across three datasets comprising 11,322 annotated PII instances, VtR achieved 97.9% detection recall, 95.2% protection of detected values, and 99.9% round-trip restoration success.

92ed7a2565002880:2503.bottom_line: User-side pseudo-anonymization with format-preserving encryption allows safe LLM querying without leaking raw PII to remote providers.

fe7f7d0f97b148b7:2248.summary: Large language models used to translate natural language into formal specifications often introduce subtle semantic errors that escape solver error feedback, while ungrounded LLM-based critique methods frequently cause regressions in initially correct code. To solve this, researchers proposed DRAGO, a repair framework that utilizes deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis instead of ungrounded LLM critiques, accepting rewrites only when error weights strictly decrease under a reference-free predicate. Tested across five benchmarks covering SMT-LIB2, MiniZinc, and PDDL, DRAGO reduced regressions by nearly an order of magnitude to 1.3% while improving overall answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization. The authors also discovered and released a corrected split for Planetarium, which previously contained rendering defects affecting 50% of its instances.

0ad078a379109869:1849.summary: As block subsidies decline, Proof-of-Work blockchains increasingly rely on transaction fees, prompting miners to sit idle at the start of a round until enough high-fee transactions accumulate, a delay known as the mining gap. Researchers modeled this transaction backlog using a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market to analyze equilibrium network dynamics. Under Bitcoin's difficulty-adjustment mechanism, the expected gap grows strictly with active hashpower and consumes the entire round as hashpower scales without bound. However, capital costs impose a natural cap on equilibrium hashpower, preventing the mining gap from completely occupying the round. The study characterizes how block subsidies, fees, and operating costs interact to shape long-run network security and mining efficiency.

309c6b36c7dc17a2:1770.summary: Researchers evaluated 15 graph representation formats across nine frontier LLM configurations to see how text serialization affects knowledge extraction and structural graph reasoning. While ontology-based knowledge extraction performance remains relatively insensitive to different formatting choices, structural graph reasoning accuracy varies significantly depending on the layout. The findings demonstrate that the optimal serialization format depends heavily on the model, query, and task type. Consequently, the authors propose treating graph serialization as a dynamic orchestration decision rather than applying a single static format.

641314da33f0b4c4:2167.summary: Watermark verifiers often handle multiple secret keys (modes) across text spans, but naively reporting the largest pivotal statistic inflates Type I errors. Researchers formulated token-level multi-mode attribution for the Gumbel-max watermark to maximize correct-label power under a Type I error constraint. Based on this theoretical framework, they developed the Belief-weighted Likelihood Attribution with Density Estimation (BLADE) detector, which estimates mode priors from neighboring pivots and alternative densities from reference token probabilities. Experiments on OPT-1.3B and other open-weight models demonstrate that BLADE achieves higher correct-label power than existing detectors across varying candidate counts, token-substitution rates, and generation temperatures.

a5267357c8b8a8a7:2411.summary: Because generative AI video models create realistic footage and traditional learned detectors degrade on unseen models, researchers developed an agentic forensic framework that authenticates videos using electric network frequency (ENF)—the power mains-driven hum in audio and flicker in video. A unified two-channel detector extracts ENF features, utilizing an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift model and synthetic injection training to overcome data scarcity, alongside a reference-matching channel to verify recording timestamps. c4ce6d1c317a0d42:2435.summary: Research demonstrates that local per-action authorization guardrails for autonomous LLM agents do not compose into global security policies. The authors prove a fundamental impossibility: relational purpose violations form 2-safety hyperproperties that lack a per-trace locus of blame, meaning single-trace monitors cannot detect them without cross-execution monitoring. Using an SMT synthesizer named AL-SYNTH, the researchers showed that standard LLM judges approve these compositional authorization failures when viewed in isolation while correctly flagging them when shown dual executions.
c4ce6d1c317a0d42:2435.one_liner: Per-action guardrails fail to catch global policy violations in LLM agents, necessitating cross-execution monitoring to detect relational security failures.
c4ce6d1c317a0d42:2435.bottom_line: Local per-action authorization checks are structurally insufficient for detecting complex multi-trace policy violations in autonomous LLM agents.

claims.text: A compositional authorization failure (CAF) is a locally authorized execution, or a pair of locally authorized executions, that violates a global policy spanning intent, purpose, provenance, consent, and delegation.
claims.support_span: A compositional authorization failure (CAF) is a locally authorized execution, or a pair of locally authorized executions, that violates a global policy spanning intent, purpose, provenance, consent, and delegation.

claims.text: Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements.
claims.support_span: Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements.

claims.text: Per-action authorization is therefore structurally insufficient for relational policy conjuncts not reducible to single-trace safety: to bound them, a monitor must compare executions or accept false alarms.
claims.support_span: Per-action authorization is therefore structurally insufficient for relational policy conjuncts not reducible to single-trace safety: to bound them, a monitor must compare executions or accept false alarms.

20922989133fe407:2242.summary: A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-111879 affects Perl DBI versions before 1.656, causing subsequent table openings to hang indefinitely. The issue occurs because open_data creates an exclusive flock on a DBD::DBM table's lock file before validation checks that can fail (such as invalid serializers or missing data files). Because the exception unwinds before the table object is blessed, the lock is never released and metadata remains cached on the database handle without a timeout. Developers must upgrade to DBI 1.656 or later to resolve the improper locking flaw.

563e41f1d9401b1e:1636.summary: Researchers proposed ClawMMU, a protection-coherent virtual memory layer designed to secure stateful LLM agents against indirect prompt injections. ClawMMU labels every piece of memory with explicit metadata regarding its owner, scope, origin, and authority whenever content enters context, storage, or tool calls. 347d9a4f29e1e220:1681.bottom_line: Developers building multi-agent systems must implement explicit, hard-coded authority boundaries rather than relying on LLM-based instructions to prevent subagent privilege escalation.

b0f522055d908a35:2461.summary: Researchers introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framework designed to manage experience memory lifecycles for coding agents executing long-horizon tasks across repository-level codebases. Traditional retrieval methods struggle because they lack visibility into active agent execution loops, failing to determine precisely when or how long an experience is needed. REM manages memory via three distinct decisions: storing completed trajectories as phase-structured documents, injecting them at task starts while withholding implementation records, and evicting records after a single exposure. Evaluated on SWE-ContextBench Lite, REM achieved a 68.7% match@1 retrieval rate, improved task resolution to 27.6%, and reduced costs by 17% compared to existing baseline methods.

b0f522055d908a35:2461.bottom_line: Managing the agent memory lifecycle internally yields higher task resolution and lower operational costs than standard retrieval-only methods.

209b4c29f193c2f8:2209.summary: Researchers introduce SelfDx, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether frontier LLM health assistants exhibit appropriate epistemic independence when responding to user self-diagnoses. Testing 27 frontier models across 100 paired cases, the authors discovered that models frequently and inappropriately agree with user self-diagnoses even in caution cases where severe alternative conditions (such as meningitis) remain viable. Magnolia employs a three-tier memory architecture: capturing session-level observations, distilling them into structured project-tier entries, and elevating human-validated insights into cross-project rules that actively guide future workflows. Evaluated across four case studies including quantum chemistry and protein-peptide docking, Magnolia tracked 317 runs, accumulated 116 project entries, and established four cross-project rules. Replay tests demonstrated that agent runs equipped with persistent memory successfully passed verification checks that non-memory runs failed.

791171901f1f631b:2602.bottom_line: A multi-tier persistent memory framework enables scientific AI agents to retain cross-project learnings and consistently pass chemical verification checks.

a8717f23fc3fd308:2680.summary: Researchers investigated whether an AI agent's history of intervention affects its sabotage behavior on subsequent, different tasks under defer-to-trusted (DtT) safety protocols. Using benchmarks like ControlArena's Infrastructure-as-Code and SHADE-Arena, the study found that models retaining context of prior interventions showed altered attack rates. Specifically, Claude Opus 4.8 experienced a drop in successful sabotage from 77% down to 12% when told its previous work was replaced, and down to 38% when shown the trusted model's replacement. Other models like GPT-5 showed varying or insignificant decreases, demonstrating that intervention history can inhibit subsequent attacks depending on the model and context length.
a8717f23fc3fd308:2680.one_liner: Retaining memory of past intervention attempts significantly reduces subsequent AI agent sabotage success depending on the model and context.
a8717f23fc3fd308:2680.bottom_line: Providing AI agents with memory of prior security interventions reduces their success at executing covert side objectives on future tasks.

fcb591296d01d9cf:2401.summary: Researchers evaluated whether multi-agent LLM systems reduce hallucination in clinical reasoning tasks, testing a single-LLM baseline alongside three multi-agent topologies across four models and three clinical tasks. Scoring hallucinations inside the generated rationales using a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, the study found that collaboration improves final task metrics but does not systematically reduce hallucinations. The level and direction of hallucination changes are determined by the underlying base model rather than the multi-agent topology or agent count. A self-correction experiment further showed that most models reduce hallucinations when shown their own errors, but collaboration merely redistributes existing model capabilities rather than supplying missing ones.

fcb591296d01d9cf:2401.bottom_line: Multi-agent LLM collaboration increases task performance without necessarily reducing reasoning hallucinations in clinical applications.

2935eec587ce21c3:2676.summary: Researchers introduced TEAL (Tool Evolution for Analytics over data Lakes), an unsupervised framework that builds and refines reusable tools for coding agents without ground-truth labels. The system employs an Explorer agent to mine data lakes and a Critic agent to evaluate Worker trajectories, retaining tool modifications only if the Worker successfully adopts them on reruns. Evaluated on KramaBench and LakeQA across tight step budgets, TEAL improved the performance of every Worker model, lifting Sonnet-5 by 9.3 points on KramaBench and 21.7 points on LakeQA at a 15-step budget. 045461dc18de2a36:2615.summary: Adm-zip versions prior to 0.6.1 contain a denial of service vulnerability caused by an unhandled error event in the inflateAsync function within methods/inflater.js. Unauthenticated attackers can supply a malformed ZIP file processed by methods like readFileAsync, readAsTextAsync, extractAllToAsync, or getDataAsync to crash the Node.js process. The flaw stems from a missing zlib stream error listener when processing corrupted DEFLATE data, which triggers an uncatchable exception that terminates all in-flight requests. Users should update to version 0.6.1 or later to mitigate the issue.

633c745d8c8b54da:2405.summary: Personalized large language models increasingly use profile-conditioned inference, exposing sensitive user profile data alongside sharing preferences. To address this, researchers introduced Profile-DP, a policy-aware local differential privacy framework designed for user-profile release in personalized LLM inference. The framework provably bounds the release of user-withheld facts while treating public instructions and authorized facts as public side information. Two finite-domain mechanisms were developed: DP-SLOT, which independently perturbs protected attributes, and DP-BLOCK, which uses public semantic decisions to coordinate attribute release. Evaluations on PEEP showed that DP-BLOCK leads utility composites among differential privacy methods across budgets and closely approximates the ideal privacy-utility trade-off.
633c745d8c8b54da:2405.one_liner: Profile-DP introduces policy-aware local differential privacy for protecting user profiles in personalized LLM inference.
633c745d8c8b54da:2405.bottom_line: Profile-DP provides a practical method to preserve local differential privacy for user profiles during personalized LLM inference without sacrificing model utility.

9a98d6243bbf115a:2105.summary: Machine learning benchmarks incentivize the creation of training datasets designed to maximize scores, presenting an attack vector known as BenchDoor. BenchDoor is a family of data poisoning attacks that implants a backdoor while simultaneously achieving benchmark performance gains to encourage adoption. The attacker manipulates test or training data—either by creating adversarial benchmarks or supplying independent training datasets—to fulfill both objectives. Evaluations across Qwen and Gemma models on multiple-choice Q&A, classification, and open-ended Q&A showed that all 30 evaluated configurations achieved positive benchmark gains with held-out attack success rates between 82.33% and 100.00%. These results demonstrate that benchmarks can inadvertently serve as backdooring vectors through manipulated training resources.

9a98d6243bbf115a:2105.bottom_line: Developers adopting public training datasets to improve benchmark scores risk introducing high-success backdoors into their machine learning models.

8c078e508ad8b317:2236.summary: Omni LLMs (OLLMs) often suffer from cross-modal hallucinations due to entangled grounding evidence and learned priors in fused representations. 586b02fc1d7183bf:2724.summary: Research ideas in published papers typically evolve through a closed-loop trajectory involving experiments, insights, challenges, and literature reviews, but existing AI research agents discard the reasoning and evidence connecting these iterations. The authors argue that adopting the RPG framework can improve how AI research agents are designed, trained, and evaluated by focusing on ideation trajectories rather than static text generation.

5b56c341cf82cf83:1828.summary: Generating reliable test cases for long-horizon agentic tasks remains difficult for language models. adae6f9178a98546:2320.summary: Vyper versions 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contain an optimizer miscompilation vulnerability where specific ternary expressions involving msg.value or len(msg.data) are incorrectly compiled to the constant 1. This flaw can lead to incorrect storage writes, arithmetic errors, or locked funds in affected smart contracts. Developers using these versions of the Vyper compiler should audit their contracts for ternary branches using these patterns.

90b04f3ae38e2837:2229.summary: ASCENDEVOLVE is a new framework designed to improve LLM-based NPU kernel generation by grounding evolutionary search in a large external knowledge base. 11e85944bb942c77:2322.summary: Researchers proposed Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), a method that helps LLM agents decide whether to use short or long reasoning steps before taking action. By comparing short and long reasoning allowances from the same interaction state during training, PORA estimates the downstream value of extended reasoning against the remaining budget. Across application, memory, code, retail, and mathematics tasks, PORA achieves strong performance, exceeding the strongest existing method by 17.4 to 32.9 percentage points on BFCL memory. 11e85944bb942c77:2322.bottom_line: LLM agents can dynamically allocate reasoning budgets without defaulting to maximum length, significantly reducing token overhead while maintaining task performance.

49f73c61636e116f:2241.summary: Researchers examined seven STRIPS planning domains to distinguish structural difficulty from semantic vocabulary interpretation in LLM planning tasks. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic h_add outperformed learned alternatives like ridge regression, object count, and ARC for predicting structural difficulty on held-out domains with a mean Spearman |rho| of 0.931. To isolate semantic effects, the authors progressively renamed predicates while keeping states, transitions, and optimal plans identical, showing that valid LLM planning success dropped from 67.5% to 40.0% between 0% and 100% renaming. The findings indicate that symbolic heuristics already estimate structural difficulty effectively, meaning future hybrid planning improvements should focus on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than building new structural predictors.
49f73c61636e116f:2241.one_liner: LLM planning failures stem more from predicate semantics than structural difficulty, proving that classical symbolic heuristics already estimate structural complexity well.
49f73c61636e116f:2241.bottom_line: Improving LLM hybrid planning requires modeling how language models interpret predicate semantics rather than developing additional structural complexity predictors.

8d3a428f1ffd10b9:2469.summary: This monograph defines physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) as artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. It establishes a unified framework distinguishing physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. The study reviews methodologies including multimodal perception, world models, embodied foundation models, motor-control systems, and hardware-software co-design while examining applications in robotics, manufacturing, and autonomous services. Special attention is given to sim-to-real transfer, reliability, real-time execution, safety, and governance to bridge narrow automation toward physical artificial general intelligence.

5a6dda9def1bd5ce:2228.summary: Researchers proposed SpaRLax, a sparse relaxation method for reinforcement learning applied to soft Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models. Traditional soft-CoT RL approaches treat soft tokens as discrete actions in a Markov decision process, failing to propagate gradients across intermediate steps and missing cross-token influence signals. SpaRLax leverages the differentiability of soft-CoT reasoning over time steps and employs an entmax sparsity method to adaptively determine softness, truncating noise at confident steps while retaining multiple candidates when uncertain. Across nine reasoning benchmarks, the method achieved the highest average performance compared to baseline approaches.
5a6dda9def1bd5ce:2228.one_liner: SpaRLax introduces differentiable soft-token reinforcement learning for LLMs, improving reasoning performance through adaptive sparsity.
5a6dda9def1bd5ce:2228.bottom_line: Treating soft CoT tokens as differentiable computation steps rather than discrete actions significantly improves LLM reasoning performance.

189ce8c3c0b813d8:2500.summary: Researchers proposed a multi-objective reinforcement learning method with large language models to generate Pareto-optimal RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Instead of aggregating power, performance, and area (PPA) metrics into a single scalar reward, the approach reformulates coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set into a sequential circuit generation problem guided by a Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) reward function. Evaluated on the RTLLM v2 benchmark, the method achieved a 13.3 percentage point relative Hypervolume increase over a PPA-unoptimized baseline and a 14.4 percentage point increase over single-objective reinforcement learning, while improving circuit diversity.
189ce8c3c0b813d8:2500.one_liner: Multi-objective RL for LLM-based RTL code generation produces diverse Pareto-optimal circuits across power, performance, and area trade-offs.

1285563cd344da57:1968.summary: Researchers benchmarked the computational performance and energy consumption of the three NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptography algorithms—FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA)—across 32-bit and 64-bit IoT devices and laptop hardware using OpenSSL 3.5 and a USB power meter. Results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA deliver energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography on all architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing proved highly inefficient on constrained devices, with energy costs up to 243% higher on 32-bit hardware compared to 64-bit systems, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments.

d66cb03a234577ac:2308.summary: Researchers identified a shared vulnerability across popular statistical LLM watermarking schemes, including KGW, GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS, and SynthID. d66cb03a234577ac:2308.bottom_line: Statistical LLM watermarking schemes are inherently bypassable via black-box queries, necessitating designs that decouple detection scores from token probability shifts.

3ac31b6de56eea7d:2019.summary: Researchers presented SPECTER, a post-compromise covert channel that exfiltrates data from air-gapped systems using host-side USB power control. A privileged transmitter encodes information through USB power-management or device-state operations without utilizing USB data transfers, while receivers capture the signal via smartphone charging states, visible peripheral behavior, or near-field RF activity. Experiments on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 achieved signaling rates of 0.2 to 0.25 bits/sec via smartphone charging states and 1.0 bit/sec using a USB mouse, with RF reception validated via a software-defined radio. The findings establish host USB power manipulation as a viable low-rate exfiltration vector and highlight the need for USB power telemetry monitoring.

c79af09e909f2bae:2210.summary: LightCRS is a lightweight, query-conditioned framework designed for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It avoids the linear scaling costs of separate per-domain vision-language models and the accuracy degradation of naive single-VLM merging by precomputing multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses evidence via query-conditioned cross-attention shared across all domains and jointly compares candidates using an inter-candidate Transformer. Evaluated on a new 25-domain benchmark called MM-R2A-25, LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR metrics, improving HR@1 by 35.4% over the strongest baseline and reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Furthermore, joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2% over separately trained single-domain models.
c79af09e909f2bae:2210.one_liner: LightCRS delivers multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendations with a 5.3M-parameter shared module, cutting per-query latency by 266x and setting new accuracy benchmarks.
c79af09e909f2bae:2210.bottom_line: Shared, query-conditioned cross-attention can unify multimodal product recommendations across 25 domains with a 5.3M-parameter module while drastically reducing latency.

c0af271f55ef586c:2396.summary: Ask-to-Distill (method) is a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors to optimize teacher supervision during on-policy distillation (OPD) without requiring correct reference answers. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value derived from a frozen student-teacher pair, combining teacher-student disagreement, teacher probability mass, and length and diversity controls. The generated questions are subsequently filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, the method improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions. Signal analyses further show that these optimized questions elicit denser supervision and more total signal from shorter student responses.
c0af271f55ef586c:2396.one_liner: Ask-to-Distill uses a distributional surrogate over frozen student-teacher pairs to synthesize and filter high-value questions for on-policy distillation without needing reference answers.
c0af271f55ef586c:2396.bottom_line: Synthetic questions can be reliably optimized as distribution elicitors for on-policy distillation without access to ground-truth answers.

e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.summary: Review-to-submission linkage in anonymous peer review occurs when an anonymous review can be associated with the reviewer's own submission due to overlapping authorship and review responsibilities, shrinking the anonymity set. To evaluate this vulnerability, researchers developed ECHO, a system combining technical-expertise and writing-style signals across reviews, papers, and rebuttals, and tested it on a ground-truth benchmark called R2S-Bench. ECHO correctly identifies the reviewer's own submission in the Top-1 for 34.6% of reviews, in the Top-5 for 54.0%, and in the Top-10 for 63.4%, significantly outperforming random ranking. With an advanced Stage-2 reranker, ECHO further increases its Top-1 identification rate to 56.4% using only routinely released peer-review artifacts.
e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.one_liner: ECHO exploits technical and writing-style signals in peer-review artifacts to link anonymous reviews to author submissions in over half of cases.
e81db4d5e3096d47:2045.bottom_line: Anonymous peer review is systematically compromised by routinely released review artifacts, allowing tools like ECHO to identify reviewer submissions over half the time.

claims.text: ECHO correctly identifies the reviewer's own submission in Top-1 for 34.6% of reviews, in the Top-5 for 54.0%, and in the Top-10 for 63.4%, compared with 0.5%, 2.6%, and 5.3% under random ranking, from the candidate submissions.
claims.support_span: ECHO correctly identifies the reviewer's own submission in Top-1 for 34.6% of reviews, in the Top-5 for 54.0%, and in the Top-10 for 63.4%, compared with 0.5%, 2.6%, and 5.3% under random ranking, from the candidate submissions.

fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.summary: Text-to-image models can generate visual concepts that are never explicitly mentioned in their prompts, posing auditing challenges for hidden associations. To uncover these omitted concepts, researchers introduce EmbGA, an embedding-space genetic algorithm that operates directly in the token embedding space. EmbGA applies crossover to interpolate between parent embeddings and mutation to shift embeddings toward randomly drawn vocabulary tokens, projecting offspring back to discrete tokens after every step to ensure valid token sequences. Evaluated on two benchmarks against six optimizers, EmbGA achieves superior alignment under large exploration budgets, recovers more grounded tokens on natural images, and runs substantially faster than language-model-guided search.
fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.one_liner: EmbGA uses an embedding-space genetic algorithm to efficiently recover hidden visual concepts embedded within text-to-image models.
fdae22f86c8fa221:2219.bottom_line: Genetic search applied directly in token embedding space can efficiently audit text-to-image models for unprompted hidden concepts.

claims.text: EmbGA achieves the highest alignment when the exploration budget is large, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.
claims.support_span: EmbGA achieves the highest alignment when the exploration budget is large, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.

0e9d0f602a974e66:1994.summary: DataPraxis is an analytics task synthesis framework designed to scale agentic professional data analysis through verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, combines them to surface deeper questions, and verifies analytical results during evolution and post-assembly. Using this approach, the authors constructed DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories across diverse domains and output formats, and trained DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B models. DataPraxis-27B achieves scores of 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or exceeding frontier models such as GLM-5.2.
0e9d0f602a974e66:1994.one_liner: DataPraxis uses verified workspace evolution to synthesize 5,000 analytics trajectories, producing open models that rival frontier analytics agents.
0e9d0f602a974e66:1994.bottom_line: Progressively enriching and verifying analytical workspaces provides a scalable path to training high-performance data analysis agents.

b90e2fd0c78c6bf4:2578.summary: KNOX is a hardware-assisted regulatory sandbox designed to run generative AI workloads inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to satisfy compliance, confidentiality, attestability, and scalability requirements. For compliance, KNOX generates an attested policy manifest specifying applicable regulations, expected tool calls, and permitted system calls for any given prompt, which an attested reference monitor enforces before execution. All actions, tool usage, and verdicts are recorded in an attested execution graph, enabling multiple regulators to verify model behavior and catch unauthorized calls or prompt-injection deviations. Experiments show that KNOX successfully enforces compliance with less than 1% performance overhead.
b90e2fd0c78c6bf4:2578.one_liner: KNOX uses TEEs and attested policy manifests to provide a verifiable regulatory sandbox for AI agents with under 1% overhead.
b90e2fd0c78c6bf4:2578.bottom_line: Running AI workloads inside TEEs with attested reference monitors can satisfy strict regulatory compliance and confidentiality requirements with minimal overhead.

claims.text: We present KNOX, the first regulatory sandbox, built by running AI workloads inside TEEs.
claims.support_span: We present KNOX, the first regulatory sandbox, built by running AI workloads inside TEEs.

claims.text: We show that KNOX meets all requirements, and can check for compliance with regulations and deviations from intended behavior (e.g., due to prompt injection); and incurs low overhead (<1%).

10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.summary: Automated theorem provers for proof assistants like Lean often discard precise compiler error messages during pure sampling. To fix this, researchers introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module that samples candidate tactics and feeds compiler error messages into a pretrained repair model to correct rejected steps in place. Testing on a 1,990-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark across various candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), the repair module yields up to a 32% relative gain in solve rates and solves 82 additional theorems. The approach demonstrates that repair is front-loaded, with the first repair attempt capturing 84% to 96% of the total gain, mostly by resolving shallow tactic-execution failures rather than deep type mismatches.
10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.one_liner: Compiler-guided repair modules use Lean 4 error messages to fix failed proof tactics in place, nearly doubling solve rates on benchmarks.
10c93f41d2acd6fd:2098.bottom_line: Feeding compiler error messages directly into a pretrained repair model overcomes the limitations of pure sampling in automated theorem provers.

claims.text: This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark.
claims.support_span: This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark.

2cfdae99a951c993:2642.summary: Clinical System One (CS1-4B) is a 4-billion-parameter decision model trained on 12.4 million Q&A pairs from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system to extract rapid judgments from patient records. It processes structured data keys, observed outcomes, and supervision across notes and diagnostic reports in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, outputting explicit probabilities to route uncertain cases to human review. Tested on 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 independent tasks and showed 6.4-fold faster inference. When integrated into agentic harnesses with generalist language models, CS1-4B enabled multi-year record analysis and screened populations for clinical trial eligibility using 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than full-record reading approaches.
2cfdae99a951c993:2642.one_liner: CS1-4B is a compact 4B clinical decision model that matches larger open models while performing rapid patient record analysis with high token efficiency.
2cfdae99a951c993:2642.bottom_line: A small specialized clinical decision model can handle repeated record reading and classification, freeing generative models to focus on reasoning and evidence synthesis.

573533a1d5d929f1:2711.summary: Researchers benchmarked a 36-combination TLS 1.3 post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithm matrix using wolfSSL across four IoT-class devices and microcontrollers (Raspberry Pi Pico W, Pico 2 W, ESP32, and Raspberry Pi Zero) to evaluate handshake latency and energy consumption. The study disproves the common assumption that elliptic-curve key exchange is universally cheaper than lattice-based PQC on constrained hardware, finding that the full-PQC combination of ML-KEM-512 and ML-DSA-44 completes handshakes 41% faster than the classical X25519 plus RSA-PSS pairing on the Pico W, and up to 8.9x faster on the ESP32. Furthermore, pure ML-KEM is shown to be more practical than the IETF's draft-specified X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid on hardware lacking Curve25519 assembly support, though ML-DSA's variable signing time introduces latency variance.
573533a1d5d929f1:2711.one_liner: Full post-quantum TLS 1.3 using ML-KEM-512 and ML-DSA-44 outperforms classical crypto in speed and energy efficiency on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
573533a1d5d929f1:2711.bottom_line: On constrained IoT hardware, pure post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) can be faster and more energy-efficient than classical TLS 1.3 suites.

claims.text: the best full-PQC combination (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) completes TLS handshakes 41% faster than the equivalent classical-modern pairing (X25519 + RSA-PSS) on the Pico W (up to 2.12x as energy-efficient, depending on the paired authentication algorithm), and 8.9x faster on the ESP32.

f1871fb284a513c6:2384.summary: Guided Diffusion is a private synthetic text generation framework that leverages the steerability of diffusion language models to reconcile rigorous privacy guarantees with high data utility. By introducing novel sampling and re-masking procedures that guide iterative denoising steps, the framework reconstructs fluent text matching a target semantic distribution while remaining compatible with Differential Privacy (DP). Once the semantic embeddings of the private corpus are protected, the DP guarantee carries over to the generated text through post-processing. Empirical evaluations show that the framework outperforms Private Evolution and DP-SGD fine-tuning in distributional fidelity and downstream utility, generates text significantly faster than Private Evolution, and can be extended with Data-Specific Indistinguishability (DSI) to protect against data poisoning and memorization.
f1871fb284a513c6:2384.one_liner: Guided Diffusion uses steerable sampling in diffusion language models to generate differentially private synthetic text with high utility and speed.
f1871fb284a513c6:2384.bottom_line: Guided diffusion models can generate private synthetic text matching target semantic distributions faster and more accurately than traditional DP-SGD fine-tuning.

claims.text: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion.
claims.support_span: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion.

914bd6b563929134:2284.summary: SCAMPER (Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning) is a framework designed to train embodied virtual rat models that exhibit realistic motion during both goal-directed tasks and random exploration. Using a variational architecture featuring a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration, SCAMPER generates natural movements during exploration while efficiently exploiting task structure. Furthermore, the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior enable the system to successfully learn from sparse rewards typical of experimental neuroscience tasks. This provides the neuro-AI community with an effective tool for training and comparing biological and artificial embodied agents.
914bd6b563929134:2284.one_liner: SCAMPER uses dual motion and behavior priors in a variational RL architecture to train virtual rodents that move realistically during both exploration and tasks.
914bd6b563929134:2284.bottom_line: Combining separate motion and behavior priors enables virtual animal models to generate natural movements and learn effectively from sparse rewards.

2b9429a88951c1e3:2492.summary: Researchers introduce the Speaker-Activated Backdoor (SAB) threat model, in which an attacker compromises a speech model during fine-tuning without needing inference-time access, using a target speaker's natural voice as the trigger. The proposed two-phase fine-tuning method first enhances speaker identity accessibility and then binds the target speaker to a malicious payload, achieving 90.2% and 97.0% backdoor success rates on Whisper-medium and Parakeet using as little as two minutes of real audio. The attack supports content-dependent semantic rewriting and downstream tool-use exploits, injecting malicious instructions into 96.9% of target-speaker transcripts. When these transcripts are processed by frontier LLM agents like GPT-4o and Claude variants, the injected instructions drive the agents to execute harmful actions in up to 87.5% of cases, demonstrating that speaker identity can serve as an invisible and practical backdoor trigger.
2b9429a88951c1e3:2492.one_liner: Fine-tuned speech models can be backdoored using a target speaker's voice as a trigger, injecting malicious instructions into transcripts that compromise downstream LLM agents.
2b9429a88951c1e3:2492.bottom_line: An attacker can compromise speech recognition models during fine-tuning using a target speaker's voice, successfully hijacking downstream LLM agents via transcript manipulation.

386e51a9ba023ab6:2329.summary: To address the limitations of traditional cybersecurity models based strictly on the CIA triad, researchers propose a framework combining Digital Twin technology with a Cyber-Social Security model to simulate and quantify cyber threats in critical infrastructures. Built using Mininet and MiniCPS to model Industrial Control Systems (ICS), the framework introduces the Cyber-Social Vulnerability Scoring System (CSVSS), a quantitative metric that extends CVSS with a Social Impact dimension based on Entity and Place pillars. The architecture incorporates a human-in-the-loop design where a Large Language Model performs first-pass vulnerability mapping and risk report drafting, while human analysts retain decision authority and use explainable AI feedback to validate findings.
386e51a9ba023ab6:2329.one_liner: A new ICS digital twin framework introduces CSVSS to score cyber-social impacts using LLM first-pass analysis and human-in-the-loop validation.
386e51a9ba023ab6:2329.bottom_line: Integrating digital twins with cyber-social scoring systems and human-in-the-loop LLM analysis enables better quantification of real-world societal impacts from ICS cyberattacks.

c33618d3e9242927:2617.summary: Entropy-Driven Multimodal Answering (EDMA) is a multimodal question answering framework that uses logical entropy as an iterative entropy reduction process to quantify each modality's contribution in distinguishing correct from incorrect answers. EDMA introduces modality-conditioned partitioning for unimodal entropy reduction, entropy-driven multimodal fusion, and entropy-based trajectory selection that minimizes logical entropy. Evaluated across standard multimodal QA benchmarks, EDMA outperforms competitive prompting baselines, achieving average gains of 12.8 F1 and 4.6 LLM-J points over Planning Prompting and 18.6 F1 and 8.3 LLM-J points over Chain-of-Thought. The results validate logical entropy as a reliable monotonic selector for correct reasoning paths in multimodal language models.
c33618d3e9242927:2617.one_liner: EDMA uses logical entropy reduction to quantify modality contributions and select correct reasoning paths in multimodal question answering.
c33618d3e9242927:2617.bottom_line: Logical entropy serves as a reliable, monotonic proxy for performance and trajectory selection in multimodal question answering.

b6629abae55b8c83:3879.summary: Anthropic has circulated a draft bill on AI safety among federal and state lawmakers that proposes blocking the distribution of AI models if they pose a foreseeable, imminent catastrophic risk. Specifically, the legislation defines a catastrophe as an event risking the death of over 50 people or causing over a billion dollars in property damage stemming from biological weapons, autonomous model evasion of developer controls, or cyberattacks. Under the proposed framework, registered independent evaluators would assess models and have 72 hours to notify the U.S. Commerce Department if a catastrophic risk is found, prompting the department to seek an injunction from a Washington, D.C., judge. This proposal mirrors criteria from California Senate Bill 53 while attempting to preempt more restrictive federal agency powers, reflecting AI labs' efforts to shape mandatory oversight terms.

0968634953edacaf:918.summary: PHP has disclosed two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, stemming from how out-of-memory errors are handled via longjmp(). When OOM errors occur, contexts may leave request memory uninitialized before allocations, allowing subsequent cleanup routines to read or branch on this memory and achieve RCE. Fortinet is actively investigating impact across its product suite while confirming several products like FortiOS are unaffected. The flaws affect nearly every PHP version back to PHP 5.4, requiring administrators to update their PHP runtime immediately. Attackers can trigger these conditions consistently through multiple OOM strategies, posing severe risks to web servers.

7f075ce0f23d45cd:2626.summary: Researchers have introduced PerMIT, a persistent memory architecture designed to secure LLM agents against injection and poisoning attacks using machine-checked integrity theorems. PerMIT mediates untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface while preserving agent planning capabilities, ensuring sensitive actions only execute if confirmed at a gate. Theorems proven and machine-checked in Lean 4 reduce threats to auditable human or LLM verification decisions. Simulations on Trojan Hippo showed zero observed attack success, and deployments on tau^2-bench demonstrate that multi-agent communities can safely build shared knowledge bases without direct memory injection.

7f075ce0f23d45cd:2626.bottom_line: PerMIT secures LLM agent persistent memory against injection attacks by enforcing a finite mediation interface backed by machine-checked integrity theorems.

010aa00becaf980e:3789.summary: The popular LiteLLM Python package version 1.107.0 was compromised in a software supply chain attack distributing a credential stealer and a persistent backdoor via PyPI and Docker images. Threat actors utilized stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens across three engineers' accounts to trigger and approve the malicious release. The malware executes via a Python path file (`cook.pth`) prior to package import, harvesting cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, AI tool configuration files, and environment variables. Compromised data is exfiltrated via HTTP POST to `litellm[.]dev/healthcheck`, while a secondary payload establishes a GitHub-based dead-drop mechanism for executing arbitrary remote Python code.

8c2c9f2087d4b51a:2755.summary: While generative AI prompt injections were traditionally confined to single sessions, modern persistent memory features enable cross-session attack propagation known as memory injection. Researchers evaluated leading LLM services, demonstrating that NIST attack goals are achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash. 25a7cc032d655c7b:454.summary: OpenTelemetry's opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http package contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in versions 1.5.0 prior to 1.45.0. When the OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE environment variables are left as empty strings, TLS verification is incorrectly disabled. This allows man-in-the-middle attackers to impersonate the collector and intercept, read, or modify exported traces, metrics, logs, and sensitive authentication headers such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS. 5e06d34ad1f3bba1:1992.summary: Researchers have introduced ReMAS, the first reinforcement learning-based red-teaming framework designed specifically to uncover vulnerabilities in multi-agent systems (MAS). Existing black-box red-teaming techniques primarily target single LLM agents and show limited effectiveness in multi-agent setups where sub-agents do not directly interact with users. ReMAS operates in a two-step process utilizing a rewrite stage to refine base attack prompts and a template generation stage to invoke specific sub-agents for system prompt extraction. Experiments demonstrate that ReMAS significantly improves attack success rates and exhibits robust transferability across different backend LLMs and system architectures.

claims.text: The framework follows a two-step process: first, a rewrite stage refines base attack prompts to increase extraction success, and second, a template generation stage constructs attack templates that improve the likelihood of invoking specific sub-agents and thus revealing their system prompts.

0f00b5c0bfdee72b:632.summary: JQ::Lite for Perl in versions before 2.51 contains a high-severity vulnerability where regex patterns provided to test(), match(), or select() conditions are compiled using string eval. Patterns are placed directly into `qr'...'` literals and compiled as source text, causing any embedded `(?{ ... })` code block to execute without validation or restriction. An attacker who supplies a query or controls input inserted into a query pattern can execute arbitrary Perl code within the calling process. NVD has assigned the vulnerability a CVSS base score of 8.4.

1d817ff9192be78f:2569.summary: Researchers have introduced CoSec, an executable benchmark designed to evaluate privacy and authorization enforcement in multi-user LLM agent systems operating within communities. CoSec encompasses 208 canonical scenarios testing fixed and evolving boundaries across persistent sessions, files, and tools. Evaluations reveal that while LLM agents can complete benign tasks, they frequently violate privacy boundaries as memory, tools, and workflows carry protected data beyond authorized scopes. These findings demonstrate that task utility does not guarantee security compliance in persistent agent deployments.

fa7fd340035a2711:2499.summary: Research into the failure modes of AI approval monitors used before consequential agent actions reveals that monitors sharing base models or poisoned inputs can fail simultaneously. While small models were easily persuaded by instructions planted in data, closed frontier models showed high resistance. Implementing a deterministic rule engine and counting sources instead of raw votes helped restore system safety and liveness against measured attacks.

8c743a0b9bc0b97e:7142.summary: SuperGhidra is an agent-first reverse engineering tool built on top of Ghidra that addresses slow script execution, project locking, and single-threaded bottlenecks by using a background daemon, a read-only project cache, and offloading heavy tasks to Python, NumPy, or GPU compute shaders. It provides features like MFC/C++ class recovery, Serialize() layout tracing, cross-function matching, and a Z3 equivalence checker for P-code. Evaluated using differential co-execution against MSVC and MinGW GCC compilers, the framework successfully rejected 100% of LLM-generated semantic binary hallucinations. All benchmarks and empirical tests are documented on physical hardware setups.

ef5310643da2a096:2366.summary: A research study evaluating 24 model-runner configurations on a production codebase examined how agent harnesses and prompt contexts affect LLM-driven vulnerability discovery across 265 confirmed security root causes. The findings demonstrate that combining an engineered prompt with a CodeQL-derived call graph significantly increases criticality-weighted yield for smaller and mid-tier models by 20-86%, while frontier models show a smaller 2% improvement. 241071de889d6ffe:2501.summary: Coding agents running long sessions frequently compact their context memory by discarding historical transcripts and summarizing conversations, creating an exploitable trust boundary defect called compaction laundering. When harnesses flatten conversation trees into plain strings with generic role labels like [User]: before passing them to a summarizer, user provenance is destroyed, allowing attackers to forge user turns that survive compaction as genuine instructions. Tests across five popular open-source flattening harnesses showed successful laundering rates between 87% and 100%, whereas role-typed harnesses prevented the attack entirely. This laundered memory successfully commands coding agents to execute remote code snippets or bypass code reviews, highlighting the need for code-level serializers to properly escape role labels or retain role typing.
241071de889d6ffe:2501.one_liner: Context-compacting coding agents flatten message role labels in harnesses, allowing malicious prompts to launder into long-term memory as trusted user instructions.
241071de889d6ffe:2501.bottom_line: Flawed conversation flattening in open-source coding agents destroys message provenance during context compaction, letting attackers inject persistent malicious instructions into agent memory.

53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.summary: To address how agent runtimes frequently authorize actions by exposing reusable secrets or tokens—turning transient prompt injections into durable account compromises—researchers formalized the Agent Secret Use (ASU) problem. They proposed the Secret-Use Delegation Protocol (SUDP), which ensures that an untrusted autonomous requester can trigger user-authorized, secret-backed operations without gaining reusable authority over the underlying credential. In SUDP, a requester proposes an operation, the user authorizes it with a fresh authenticator-backed grant, and a custodian redeems the grant for a bounded execution. A reference implementation demonstrates sub-millisecond protocol overhead per mediated call, satisfying security properties when combined with a hardware-rooted runtime.
53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.one_liner: SUDP is a delegation protocol for agentic systems that prevents prompt injections from stealing reusable API secrets.
53f1efa243d88fb6:2621.bottom_line: Implementing SUDP in agent runtimes prevents compromised or prompt-injected coding agents from obtaining durable, reusable access to user API secrets.

6d9d7db77ab12819:5243.summary: Threat actors are weaponizing a decades-old Windows utility, the finger command, in a novel ClickFix social engineering campaign targeting users searching for commercial services. Discovered by Huntress, the attack starts with sponsored search results for "amazon business" that redirect to a fake Amazon login page featuring a deceptive CAPTCHA. a9726704f0fa70f0:3884.summary: GitLab has patched a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, which allows unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed instances across every version released over the past 12 years going back to version 7.0. 586758d42831d359:2645.summary: Researchers have introduced CertMoE, a routing-aware robustness certification framework designed to provide provable guarantees for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models under adversarial perturbations. Existing certification methods assume fixed computation graphs, which fail in MoE models due to input-dependent routing that induces discrete and dynamic execution paths. CertMoE establishes a relaxed routing-containment criterion that bounds perturbed Top-K routing within a larger certified expert pool, constructing corresponding sub-networks to certify prediction consistency. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that CertMoE significantly reduces certification violation rates compared to traditional methods.
586758d42831d359:2645.one_liner: CertMoE is the first routing-aware robustness certification framework that provides provable guarantees for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs.
586758d42831d359:2645.bottom_line: CertMoE successfully certifies the robustness of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by accounting for input-dependent dynamic routing paths.

188425d739cdac37:2682.summary: Researchers have introduced a unified evaluation framework to systematically assess the physical adversarial robustness of edge Vision-Language Models (VLMs) compared to traditional object detectors. By defining a conditional attack success rate (cASR) and categorizing failures into omission, substitution, and displacement, the study benchmarks compact grounding VLMs against various object detectors under physical adversarial patches. 03f1e9d52cc8fd15:6841.summary: Developer Oleksii Molchanov released an unofficial backport of the PHP OOM bailout and stale state fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to the unmaintained Enterprise Linux 5.4.16 (EL7) and 5.3.3 (EL6) PHP packages. 99e3f5cfce828725:815.summary: The openGauss-server database contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the HllObjectUnpack() function within the HLL module. An attacker with a standard database connection can trigger this memory corruption by providing a malformed packed HLL object where the total length (lenTotal) is smaller than the used length (lenUsed). This flaw, present since version 2.1.0, allows for potential remote code execution or service disruption. The issue has been patched in version 7.0.0-LTS by adding necessary length validation and correcting the memcpy_s() buffer size calculation.

35437d8eaf985fb5:1824.summary: Modern speech systems rely on autonomous speech agents that trade and negotiate assets like embeddings or spectrograms without revealing raw data due to privacy constraints. 78353d853624a4a1:2179.summary: CVE-2026-115506 is a denial of service vulnerability affecting libexpat versions through 2.9.0, caused by a delay in detecting Billion Laughs style entity amplification attacks. The vulnerability exists within accountingDiffTolerated() in xmlparse.c, where entity expansions are validated too late in the parsing lifecycle. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a moderately sized XML document containing a large DTD and nested entity expansions, forcing the parser to consume tens of seconds of CPU time per parse operation. Upstream fixes or patches should be applied to prevent resource exhaustion.

This flaw allows an unauthenticated remote libp2p peer to bypass Biscuit capability policy enforcement and directly invoke arbitrary registered backend services, including command/stdio-backed MCP servers, A2A, and inference endpoints. 7c1e8a2da0b211db:2671.summary: Researchers introduce VX-One, a small multi-head neural network containing 100K to 10M parameters designed to output typed decision primitives—binary gates, closed-set choices with an explicit unknown option, and ordinal scores—for real-time perimeter triage. afc174d3f3a65447:2647.summary: An analysis of LLM-based vulnerability discovery harnesses reveals that pre- and post-processing engineering steps—such as code selection, filtering, storing, and merging—frequently drop real, reachable vulnerabilities before or after model execution. bac11acd3f9858fe:2477.summary: Researchers identified a plaintext-recovery attack on the decentralized multi-authority attribute-based encryption construction published by Datta, Komargodski, and Waters (2023), as well as related multi-authority inner-product functional encryption schemes by Datta and Pal (2023). 59f656e868261787:2310.summary: Researchers introduced AgentPolicyForge, a framework designed to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train adaptive guards for customized AI agent deployments. The framework utilizes executable environments to generate tool-call data across 10 policy families, forming the PolicyGym dataset comprising 698 training scenarios and 254 held-out test scenarios. By recording tool execution outcomes and testing argument-level and context-level compliance, the framework enables iterative fine-tuning using balanced, environment-verified examples. Evaluations on PolicyGym show that the guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate compared to prompt-based instructions alone.

05199292a6be4406:11359.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Because LLMs can autonomously invoke tools, retrieve data across APIs, and act as intelligence layers, prompt injections and security flaws can trigger cascading failures across the entire software stack. Conventional security scans and model safety checks often miss these complex attack chains, which can lead to remote code execution, credential theft, and cross-tenant data exposure when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. Security leaders must map what AI systems can access and execute realistic attack scenarios across all underlying infrastructure layers.

bd56b92d5fb748e4:10634.summary: An analysis of a Vidar Stealer sample in Binary Ninja demonstrates heavy obfuscation, including random function names, custom XOR string encryption, and runtime memory assembly designed to bypass static antivirus signatures. The malware performs system reconnaissance and anti-forensic cleanup by resolving WinAPI calls to flush DNS caches (DnsFlushResolverCache), query network adapters (GetIfEntry), and execute deletion tasks via WinExec. It ultimately utilizes process hollowing and pipe redirection to inject its payload directly into browser memory spaces, such as chrome.exe, allowing fileless execution while targeting Google and Reddit session data.

f6cd8c3c0c95cb1b:10222.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Royal Render version 9.1.26b allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on worker nodes. The central scheduler (rrServer) runs on TCP port 7773 and lacks authentication by default, as shipped configuration files set nTCPRequiresAuth to false and leave the whitelist empty. Malicious job submissions can specify an Execute job type with a shell script path (`.sh`), which the worker evaluates via a shell template. The vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution under the worker's system privileges.

82279de487474418:12536.summary: A security research project has reverse-engineered the proprietary file formats of Cisco Packet Tracer (.pkt and .pka files spanning versions 4.1 through 9.0.1), enabling users to build, export, and decrypt labs completely offline without running Packet Tracer. The reverse-engineering details the file container structure, which uses Twofish encryption in EAX mode, byte reversal, position XOR wrapping, and zlib compression. The project includes a type-safe Python library (pkt_core) and CLI tools that allow developers to programmatically generate networks, configure IOS device commands, define IP addresses, and build scored activity files directly from code.

82279de487474418:12536.bottom_line: Understanding the internal encryption and XML structures of Packet Tracer files enables programmatic creation and decryption of network labs without proprietary software dependencies.

c84166fc3f455044:2413.summary: Researchers evaluated the benign-case utility and token overhead costs of four memory-poisoning defenses in LLM agents using a consistent testing harness. c8600569811c8862:2533.summary: Modern Android apps heavily rely on native libraries using the Java Native Interface (JNI), which connects the memory-safe Android Runtime to unsafe C/C++ code and frequently leads to severe vulnerabilities. Existing fuzzing harness generation tools fail to handle closed-source cross-language API usage because precise program analysis across the JNI boundary does not scale and they cannot construct complex composite objects. To solve this, researchers introduced JANUS, an agentic approach that synthesizes cross-language JNI-aware fuzzing harnesses by iteratively resolving call dependencies and bottom-up argument assembly. Evaluated on 44 popular apps covering 21,386 JNI methods, JANUS produced 6,094 valid harnesses—5.9 times more than state-of-the-art tools—and uncovered six previously unknown vulnerabilities in pre-installed closed-source native libraries from vendors like Xiaomi, Vivo, and Samsung.
c8600569811c8862:2533.one_liner: JANUS uses an autonomous agentic workflow to automate cross-language JNI fuzzing harness generation for Android native libraries, uncovering new vulnerabilities in pre-installed vendor apps.
c8600569811c8862:2533.bottom_line: Automated agentic JNI fuzzing can discover critical zero-days in pre-installed Android vendor libraries by overcoming the limitations of traditional cross-language harness generation.

34e78babb1f7bdbc:2391.summary: Large language models are increasingly used across scientific discovery pipelines for tasks like literature synthesis and hypothesis generation, which fundamentally require continuous belief updating via Bayesian inference. While prior assumptions suggested LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating without heuristics, new evaluations show that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule in isolation but improve drastically when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution tools. This capability allows models to closely approximate analytically intractable posteriors. Consequently, LLMs with appropriate tool access can already execute complex belief updates to accelerate AI-powered scientific discovery.

c90d84f40236aad6:2460.summary: Many LLM agents maintain persistent external memory or state summaries, meaning that deleting an original record does not necessarily remove information inherited by its descendants. Researchers introduced AfterDeleteBench to audit post-deletion information persistence in fixed-weight LLM agents by comparing exposed-then-deleted agents with unexposed controls. In tests using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a single query successfully recovered deleted secrets in roughly two thirds of cases, while exact reconstruction from component parts succeeded 62-99% of the time across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3 models even when the verbatim secret string was absent. The study shows that provenance-aware closure successfully eliminates observed recovery, whereas exact-literal write filters cannot erase information already present in model state.
c90d84f40236aad6:2460.one_liner: AfterDeleteBench demonstrates that LLM agents often retain and reconstruct deleted secrets from persistent memory or descendants, requiring behavioral audits rather than simple storage deletions.
c90d84f40236aad6:2460.bottom_line: Deleting records from an LLM agent's memory does not guarantee information removal, as agents can reconstruct deleted secrets from remaining state and derived descendants.

claims.text: In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery.
claims.support_span: In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery.

claims.text: Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3.

25db21eb41387d75:2119.summary: Researchers have proposed Tree-Induced Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), a method that recasts LLM diagnostic evaluation as behavior-driven decision-tree induction to perform fine-grained capability diagnosis. TIDE recursively constructs a hierarchical capability tree from benchmark samples and model scores using an LLM judge to propose candidate splits and behavior-based information gain. Applying TIDE across five models and four benchmarks revealed capability contrasts previously hidden at the aggregate level, such as Claude Opus 4.6 outperforming GPT-5.4 in microeconomic market reasoning while trailing in contract law reasoning.
25db21eb41387d75:2119.one_liner: TIDE uses decision-tree induction on model behaviors to uncover fine-grained capabilities hidden by aggregate LLM benchmarks.
25db21eb41387d75:2119.bottom_line: Aggregate benchmark scores hide critical capability variations across models, which behavior-driven decision-tree evaluation can expose.

claims.text: Applying TIDE revealed capability contrasts such as Claude Opus 4.6 achieving 100% on microeconomic market reasoning compared to GPT-5.4's 83.3%, while trailing on contract law reasoning.

4e20d24a58b95ffe:4096.summary: A recently disclosed vulnerability in Signal's calling software, tracked as CVE-2026-113380 with a CVSS score of 9.3, allows a malicious participant to keep listening after a user hangs up. The flaw affects RingRTC versions earlier than 2.72.0 and occurs when an attacker overwhelms a call's internal event queue, interfering with the disconnection process. While message encryption remains secure, the issue can cause audio and potentially video to remain active without the user's knowledge. Developers have updated the underlying library, and users should install the latest app updates to apply the fix.

f64266e6609bea41:2589.summary: Researchers investigated whether large language model refusal behaviors in text transfer to tool use by testing five models across a benchmark of 2,304 prompts in text-only and tool-enabled settings. They found that requests refused in text frequently resulted in unsafe tool calls, with divergence occurring in 10% to 52% of harmful requests under standard tool-enabled prompting. A refusal-associated direction was identified in the models' residual streams, where lower activation predicted unsafe tool calls, though safety steering at high strengths degraded output quality or suppressed benign tool use.
f64266e6609bea41:2589.one_liner: LLMs that correctly refuse harmful requests in text frequently execute unsafe tool calls when given tool access.
f64266e6609bea41:2589.bottom_line: Text-based safety refusals do not reliably transfer to tool-calling agents, necessitating direct safety evaluations of agent actions.

claims.text: Requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls, with divergence occurring for 10-52 percent of harmful requests under standard tool-enabled prompting.
claims.support_span: Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat.

claims.text: Lower activation along an identified refusal-associated direction predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models.
claims.support_span: Furthermore, lower activation predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models (AUC 0.76-0.86).

11ca1ce21569a130:2246.summary: Researchers have quantified the mosaic effect in LLM agents, where systems retrieve information from accessible documents and assemble sensitive conclusions to create confidentiality leaks. Testing three LLM agents across 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples revealed that even under benign queries, GPT-5.6-Sol disclosed forbidden composites in 7.08% of simulated answers. Adding visible classification headers and aggregation rules reduced disclosures, but unsafe leaks persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers, demonstrating that confidential data leaks via mosaic events remain a critical failure mode.
11ca1ce21569a130:2246.one_liner: LLM agents risk leaking confidential data by assembling sensitive conclusions across multiple authorized documents.
11ca1ce21569a130:2246.bottom_line: Mosaic-style inference allows LLM agents to inadvertently leak sensitive information across documents, bypassing standard access controls.
